item.title: USC shocks No. 2 Ohio state to keep CFP hopes alive
item.description: Mark Bowman #19 of the USC Trojans hurdles a defender during an NCAA football game against the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday, October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, CA. LOS ANGELES – After the product that showed up on the field last weekend against Wisconsin, Halloween night at the Coliseum seemed like it might get scary for Lincoln Riley and USC . Yet, with the outside criticism at its loudest in quite some time, the program had an answer. The Trojans pulled off a stunning 30-18 upset over the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday night, giving their slim College Football Playoff hopes a glimpse of light. "Great atmosphere in the Coliseum," head coach Lincoln Riley said. "Super proud of the team. The players, the staff, everybody stayed together through the week...that's why [it's] a pretty happy locker room right now." Riley faced a plethora of questions regarding his job security from the media and fans after his team’s seven points in Madison represented their lowest single-game point total throughout his tenure with the team thus far. Despite the heat, he remained firm in his belief that USC is where he’s meant to be, and being the head coach of the Trojans is the right job for him. No matter how much reassurance he wished to provide, Saturday’s victory against the Buckeyes will go much further than any words ever could have. It was wire-to-wire, confident football from the Trojans as they never trailed for a single moment. "Every week's a battle," Riley said. "What you did last week doesn't matter, and what you do next week doesn't matter. Every game is its own season." That’s largely due to the part of Trent Mosley, who provided the type of tone-setter that USC desperately needed in front of its home crowd. On the second play from scrimmage, he took a screen pass from Jayden Maiava and ran it 69 yards to the house to send the Coliseum into a frenzy. Maiava finished the day with 222 yards passing, completing 15 of 22 passes. Just how effective was the freshman? He outdueled Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith, who caught 10 overall passes for 83 yards. He was the only wide receiver on the team to finish with more than one reception. Fortunately for the Trojans, it didn’t matter. item.title: Hailie Deegan wins ARCA West finale as Huddleston claims another championship
item.description: Motorsport photo After just 42 laps of racing, inclement weather prevented ARCA Racing officials from completing the final 108 laps at Kevin Harvick's Kern Raceway, with Hailie Deegan earning the win in a rain-shortened season finale. Deegan was part of a historic all-female front row with pole-sitter Mia Lovell, and she ultimately finished second to Deegan to make a little bit more history. This is also the first time in series history where female swept the top two positions in a race. "It's been super awesome in the race," said Deegan, who also won at Madera earlier this year. "Overall, I was mad at qualifying -- 0.007s (from pole), so, I was frustrated with myself, but we were able to get the lead quick and checked out from there. So, had a really good car. Felt like I wasn't using up too much tires. Wish we could have gotten more laps, and I was having a blast out there, but we'll take it." Deegan now has five career victories in the ARCA West Series, tying her with current NASCAR names like Jesse Love, Noah Gragson, William Sawalich, and Taylor Gray. ✌️ wins in ‘26 @HailieDeegan ‼️ https://t.co/SF5fh3K4UO — ARCA Menards Series (@ARCA_Racing) November 1, 2026 Huddleston takes the crown again Hudson Sharp finished third in Saturday's rain-shortened race, Taylor Mayhew fourth, and Trevor Huddleston fifth. Huddleston earned the 2026 ARCA West championship, and he and Deegan were the only drivers to win multiple races. Huddleston also won the 2025 ARCA West championship, going back-to-back. "Awesome Victory Lane for many reasons, obviously being out here at Kevin Harvick's Kern Raceway," said Huddleston after the event. "It's a very unique Victory Lane because it's pouring rain. It felt like we weren't going to race at all today, but we got some laps in and we brought it home and that's all that counts. item.description: Texas Longhorns linebacker Rasheem Biles (3) celebrates an interception with teammates Zina Umeozulu (19) and Justin Cryer (28) against Mississippi in the second quarter at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) The Texas Longhorns have a blueprint to success. It's not sexy but when done well, it will keep them in the running for a spot in the College Football Playoff. It's a wildly offensive (in a points-scoring way) era in the sport but the Longhorns are a defensive minded ballclub that will go into each game knowing that a more conservative approach can possibly defy some rough odds to get them to the postseason. MORE CEDDY: Why SEC coaches were nervous adding a ninth league game If they're going anywhere, it will be the defense that leads. That's no news flash but it bears repeating every game for the rest of this season. Saturday's 31-3 win over Mississippi State was a perfect illustration of what powers this group. Quarterback Arch Manning made some nice throws - he tossed three touchdowns - and used his legs more than he has in any game this season, but it was all about the hard-nosed defense shutting down the banged-up Bulldogs over four quarters of rough and tumble ball. MORE HORNS: Texas loses WR Cam Coleman again Maraad Watson, a 333-pound defensive tackle who earns his paycheck in contained spaces, went the long-distance route with a 61-yard fumble recovery for a touchdown to put a game that was never in doubt out of reach in the second quarter. item.title: Dave Portnoy ruthlessly mocks Angel Reese with video after WNBA Finals loss
item.description: Credit: Erica Denhoff/Icon Sportswire/Ezra Shaw via Getty Images One of Angel Reese’s most vocal haters, Dave Portnoy is letting the WNBA superstar hear about it on social media after the Atlanta Dream’s Finals loss. Dave Portnoy is at times one of the most divisive and controversial personalities on social media, and nothing encapsulates that more than his WNBA takes. The Barstool CEO has spoken time and again about his dislike for WNBA superstar Angel Reese, going all the way back to her LSU days. Portnoy and other Caitlin Clark fans like him were almost in for a tough summer when it looked like Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream might just win the WNBA championship. The 24-year-old would have been the favourite to win Finals MVP, too. That’s not how things turned out, so Dave has been quick to gloat. Dave Portnoy takes ‘0-1 lifetime’ dig at Angel Reese, shares lowlights video It was a mixed bag in the Finals for the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Reese had arguably two of her career’s finest performances in Games 2 and 3 to give Atlanta the series lead. However, she also came up short quite a bit, scoring less than 10 points in three out of the seven games. Angel shot below 30 percent from the field in three games, which means there are numerous clips of her missing shots from the Finals. Portnoy shared a compilation of the same on X along with a jab. “Yoooo… Who made this video? Angel 0-1 lifetime in WNBA Finals,” Portnoy wrote in his post to go along with several laughing emojis. The video itself shows Reese talking about winning a title and clips of her talking trash on the court. It is then followed up with her air balls, misses, and turnovers from the Finals. Portnoy represents what Angel and the Dream will have to deal with a lot this offseason. There is no rivalry in modern sports as fiercely fought by fans online as the one between Clark and Reese’s fans. No doubt, Angel’s supporters will keep these receipts for when the Atlanta star eventually does win. item.title: Saturday Tourney Roundup: St. Thomas, Portsmouth Christian volleyball advance
item.description: DOVER - The St. Thomas Aquinas volleyball team was pushed to the brink Saturday night, but the fourth-seeded Saints refused to let their season end. After dropping the first two sets, St. Thomas stormed back to win three straight and defeat No. 5 Trinity, 3-2, in a Division III quarterfinal. The Saints lost the opening two sets, 25-21 and 25-15, before turning the match around. St. Thomas won the third set, 25-17, stayed alive with a 25-22 victory in the fourth and completed the comeback with a 15-9 win in the decisive fifth set. “Tonight was a tough game,” St. Thomas coach Kristie Holtz said. “Trinity was relentless. We are so proud of our girls. We didn’t give up even after losing the first two sets.” STA will face top-seed Portsmouth Christian Academy on Thursday in a semifinal game at Oyster River High School. The victory sends St. Thomas to the Division III semifinals after the Saints found themselves just one set away from elimination. “We are excited to keep the season going and focused on the next round,” Holtz said. Hadley DeStefano led the Saints with 17 kills and 18 digs, while Jules Stowell contributed with 10 kills, 15 digs and 22 assists. VOLLEYBALL No. 1 Portsmouth Christian Academy 3 No. 8 Inter-Lakes 2 DOVER - Top-seeded Portsmouth Christian (16-1) won the first two sets before Inter-Lakes rallied to force a decisive fifth set. The Eagles prevailed with set scores of 25-23, 25-8, 18-25, 13-25 and 15-11 in a Division III quarterfinal. Molly Marquis led PCA with 13 kills, seven aces and 13 digs, while Dylan Anderson added 13 kills and four blocks. Bea Monahan contributed 10 kills, four aces and 18 digs, and Caroline Braman finished with eight kills. Lexi Jordan directed the offense with 38 assists while adding two aces and 10 digs. item.title: USC's stunning upset over No. 2 Ohio State saves Lincoln Riley from Halloween disaster
item.description: USC's stunning upset over No. 2 Ohio State saves Lincoln Riley from Halloween disaster originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayden Maiava passed for 222 yards and a touchdown while Trent Mosley racked up 145 all-purpose yards as Southern California stunned No. 2 Ohio State 30-18 on Saturday at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Ohio State started true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey in place of the injured Julian Sayin, but the Trojans (7-2, 4-2 Big Ten) dictated terms from the opening snap. Just 39 seconds into the game, Mosley took a short screen from Maiava and raced untouched down the sideline for a 69-yard touchdown. Late in the first quarter, Mosley set up USC’s second score with a 44-yard punt return to the Ohio State 46, helped by a Buckeyes personal foul. Two plays after hauling in a 14-yard reception, Mosley watched Waymond Jordan scamper into the end zone from 9 yards out to extend the lead to 14-3. USC pushed its advantage to 17-6 on Ryon Sayeri’s career-long-tying 54-yard field goal. Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) was repeatedly forced to settle for field goals in the red zone, as Connor Hawkins converted kicks of 39, 34, and 23 yards—the last coming after the Buckeyes stalled with a first-and-goal at the USC 1-yard line—to send the Trojans into halftime leading 20-9. Maiava finished 15-of-22 passing, while Mosley caught five passes for 101 yards. MORE: ​ Week 10 college football first look USC broke the game open midway through the third quarter. After Ohio State's West fumbled and Floyd Boucard recovered at the Buckeyes' 32-yard line, Maiava connected with Mark Bowman on a 70-yard catch-and-run that set up King Miller’s 1-yard touchdown plunge to make it 27-9. Fahey completed 21 of 38 passes for 260 yards and a touchdown. Jeremiah Smith recorded 10 catches for 83 yards, capping his day with a 1-yard touchdown grab with 2:12 remaining. The score marked Smith’s 40th career Big Ten receiving touchdown, tying ex-Michigan’s Braylon Edwards for the most in conference history. MORE: Luke Fahey stats today Following a failed two-point conversion that kept it 27-18, USC's Tanook Hines scooped up the Buckeyes' onside kick and returned it 24 yards to the Ohio State 21. Caden Chittenden sealed the victory with a 32-yard field goal with 1:46 left. item.title: Five Oklahoma State football takeaways after Iowa State overwhelms Cowboys' defense
item.description: AMES — For a change, Oklahoma State 's offense put the defense in a tough spot. OSU fell to Iowa State 51-49 . OSU tied the game with 53 seconds left on a misdirection pitch pass to Wyatt Young. Just a couple plays after being on the receiving end of an unnecessary roughness call, Young ran to the Iowa State stands in his celebration and received an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on the play that was assessed on the kickoff. Cowboy Joseph Kim kicked off from the 15-yard line and got the ball to the other 15. Cyclone Carson Robbins' 22-yard return set ISU up from the 37. A 33-yard pass to freshman receiver Jamal Polite got strong-legged kicker Kyle Konrardy in field-goal range. Konrardy made a game-winning 34-yard field goal as time expired. OSU's defense struggled throughout much of the second half and gave up 27 points after halftime. Iowa State put up 581 total yards of offense, passing for 309 and rushing for 272. Iowa State ran four plays that gained least 40 yards. This was the same Cyclone team that scored three points and accumulated 221 total yards last week against Arizona. item.title: Chiefs’ pursuit of Tyreek Hill faces fresh uncertainty ahead of trade deadline
item.description: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs’ chances of reuniting with Tyreek Hill appear to be fading as concerns over the wide receiver’s fitness and legal situation complicate a potential return. Kansas City have been looking for ways to strengthen their receiving options for Patrick Mahomes, but Hill remains unsigned despite the franchise making initial contact with him weeks ago. With the NFL trade deadline approaching, the Chiefs are also exploring other options to address their needs at wide receiver, potentially reducing the likelihood of a reunion with their former star. Tyreek Hill’s fitness and off-field pressure complicate Kansas City Chiefs return Jonathan Jones of The Athletic recently provided an update on Kansas City’s search for a wide receiver, highlighting the team’s continued interest in the position. “We’re still keeping a close watch on the Chiefs and wide receivers,” Jones wrote. “There’s a clear need there, even with the hope that Tyquan Thornton will be back for the playoffs (and even with the ever-present possibility of signing Tyreek Hill).” However, ESPN’s Ian Rapoport suggested that Hill’s current situation could make a deal difficult. “Tyreek Hill is not healthy enough, and there’s obviously all the off-field stuff,” Rapoport reported. Hill has been recovering from a serious leg injury sustained early last season. He also recently faced legal issues reportedly, involving his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro. The court awarded Vaccaro $500,000. There is also the possibility of NFL disciplinary action following the civil case, although no suspension has been confirmed. Kansas City do not need to trade for Hill because he is currently a free agent. However, his fitness and the wider circumstances surrounding him could influence whether the Chiefs decide to bring him back. Meanwhile, the franchise could pursue alternative targets, with Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Minnesota Vikings wideout Jauan Jennings mentioned as potential trade options. A move for another receiver would make Hill’s return less necessary, particularly with Rashee Rice expected to return from a hamstring issue and Thornton working towards a comeback from an ankle dislocation. The Chiefs still need help at the position, but their next move could determine whether Hill remains a realistic option or becomes a missed opportunity for Mahomes and Kansas City. item.title: Angel Reese had a statement season, just not the last word in the WNBA Finals
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO – Her manifestation met but unfulfilled, Angel Reese walked expressionless up the tunnel on Saturday as confetti fell for the other team, closer to who she wants to be but at least another year from getting there. Making the WNBA Finals was never the point of her long-ago social media post about making the WNBA Finals. She launched that idea into the universe last October as an implication. The Atlanta Dream star wishes to conquer this world and take her place in a forever pantheon, and she is acutely aware that winning championships is the only way to do it, and everything else is a preface to the story. That was the weight dragging emotion from Reese’s face as she left the Chase Center floor. That was the burden still pushing tears to the edge of her eyes a long time after. A 68-63 loss in Game 7 to the Golden State Valkyries was a cosmic interruption. She came this close to the front of the line for her generation, leaving everyone else to crane their necks behind the velvet rope. One more victory, and Reese’s peers chase her legacy by following the light reflecting off her championship ring. “To be considered a superstar, to be considered one of the best,” Reese declared before the game, underlining everything she’s believed for a while now, “you have to win.” The highest stakes, she said. That’s what this night was. And while she didn’t articulate it out loud, there was this, too: All the arrows shot in her direction — and there are enough of them to blot out the sky — are waved away by bringing a title to Atlanta more or less immediately after she brought herself to Atlanta. A special delivery, courtesy the woman they introduce as The Queen of the South before home games, even though that part of the South has been her Queen-dom for all of seven months. As it is, validation remains in the eye of the beholder. Reese was a second-team all-WNBA honoree for 2026, the first time she has earned a place among that coterie. She finished seventh, albeit by a large distance, in MVP voting. She came to Atlanta fully aware of her limitations, and only started to fix those. She came to Atlanta to win a title , and only got eight of the nine wins required. She turned 24 in May. She is not done. The distance between here and there, though, will define her. “This is the most fun I’ve ever had with a group,” Reese said after the game. “It’s the most competitive team I’ve ever been a part of, where everybody just wants to see each other get better. item.title: The Buckeyes Won the Box Score But Lost the Football Game Against USC
item.description: It was a thorough beatdown of the Ohio State Buckeyes at the hands of the USC Trojans on Saturday night in Los Angeles. That's what our eyes told us, but the box score tells a completely different story. If you were to just look at the box score from Saturday's game against USC, you would think that the Buckeyes won this football game by two or three scores. It would be hard to believe that the opposite is true. The Buckeyes outgained the Trojans by nearly 130 yards; the Buckeyes were much better on third down; they averaged almost a half yard more on the ground; they out-rushed the Trojans by almost 100 yards; they had nearly 40 minutes of possession to USC's nearly 20. No matter what stat you look at, the Buckeyes won the category. However, they lost the football game and lost it handily. There are a couple of reasons why that is the case, but there is also a conversation to be had that a result like this should never exist. When everything gets boiled down, the Trojans executed when the chips were down, and the Buckeyes did not. Instant Analysis: Buckeyes Fall to the USC Trojans on the Road, Season Put Squarely on the Brink The Ohio State Buckeyes went west to Los Angeles and took on the USC Trojans, and they were beaten thoroughly, up and down the field for four quarters as the... The number one sequence in the entire game is when quarterback Luke Fahey was tagged down at quite literally the one-foot line. The Buckeyes had first and goal from inside the one, and you guessed it, they kicked a field goal. That sequence was part of USC bowing up, but also the Buckeyes tripping over themselves in a significant way. It was a false start that pushed the Buckeyes back, and then three straight neutral plays led to a field goal kick right before the half. Then, the Buckeyes came out of halftime, and the ensuing drive went run, run, run, punt to begin the half. At that point, it felt like the Buckeyes resigned themselves to needing a miracle to win a game that was more than winnable. Even the final drive of the football game, the Buckeyes needed to score quickly and instead of pushing the tempo and going with urgency, they went on a 13-play, 80-yard drive that took 5:45 seconds off the clock. Midway through that drive, it was more than obvious that the Trojans were so happy with them just casually taking the ball up the field. They were happy with trading 80 yards and 7 points for nearly a 3rd of the quarter. At the end of the day, Ryan Day was outcoached by Lincoln Riley to the point that now the Buckeyes' future with one of the best players to ever play the sport of college football is totally in question. It was a disastrous evening for the Buckeyes, and now their backs are against the wall. It is put-up-or-shut-up time in Columbus, and they have zero wiggle room. Ryan Day, we will see what you are made of.
